name: Botswanan Seswaa
description: Seswaa, beef slow-boiled until tender enough to shred by hand, is widely considered Botswana's national dish, traditionally cooked outdoors in a large pot for gatherings.
steps_detailed: Simmer the beef with the onion and enough water to cover, 1.5-2 hours, until completely fork-tender.
Shred the beef by hand or with two forks.

name: Botswanan Bogobe
description: Bogobe, a soft sorghum porridge, is Botswana's most essential staple starch, traditionally eaten for breakfast or alongside seswaa.
steps_detailed: Whisk the sorghum flour into 1.5 cups boiling water.
Cook, stirring often, 15-18 minutes until thick and smooth.
steps: Whisk the sorghum flour into 1.5 cups boiling water.
Cook, stirring often, 15-18 minutes until thick and smooth.

name: Botswanan Morogo
description: Morogo, wild or cultivated leafy greens cooked simply, a genuine Botswanan staple side.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion 4-5 minutes, then add the tomatoes and simmer 3-4 minutes.
Add the kale and simmer 10-12 minutes until tender.

name: Botswanan Seswaa Chicken
description: A chicken version of Botswana's beloved seswaa technique, slow-simmered until tender enough to shred.
steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken with the onion and enough water to cover, 30-35 minutes, until very tender.
Shred the chicken by hand or with two forks.

name: Botswanan Fat Cakes (Magwinya)
description: Magwinya, fried dough balls, a beloved Botswanan snack closely related to South African vetkoek.

Let rest 15 minutes.
Shape into small balls and fry, turning, 4-5 minutes per batch, until deeply golden.
